# Crawlable links

Google extracts links from a page's HTML ('We like links.') to discover pages, understand site structure and rank, sending new URLs back to the crawl queue, which extends Day 1's point that discovery runs on links. Only an a element whose href holds a real URL is dependable: Google's slide put onclick-only links (Googlebot does not click, as on Day 1), routerLink without href, href on a span and javascript: URLs under 'can not extract', while its documentation calls them not recommended and says Google may still try to parse them. Links are extracted before and after rendering, so JavaScript-added a href links can count, but a community speaker showed navigation that exists only after rendering being lost when rendering fails. Day 2 repeats Day 1 on fragments: Google cannot request the part of a URL after #, which Google called the next most common JavaScript issue, so single-page apps should use real paths with the History API, a change it called not free but relatively straightforward. A community speaker showed a language selector built as a button that orphaned a whole set of language versions; Google said it sometimes extracts plain-text URLs too, but that passage of the recording is unclear. Day 3 timed link processing: Google estimated that link annotations are processed in minutes to 1-3 weeks, with an end point of about a year (not in Google's docs), and an audience member's large site showed recrawl frequency following site hierarchy and internal linking. In the Day 1 Q&A Google said that if paginated pages are replaced by a load-more button or infinite scroll without crawlable links, Google will not see the further pages at all; on Day 2 migration speakers stressed updating internal links so moved pages do not rely on redirects alone.

Based on: `D2-C036`, `D2-C038`, `D2-C048`, `D1-C040`, `D2-C039`, `D2-C040`, `D1-C115`, `D2-C041`, `D2-C042`, `D2-C043`, `D2-C287`, `D2-C168`, `D2-C169`, `D2-C140`, `D1-C101`, `D2-C284`, `D2-C283`, `D2-C285`, `D2-C185`, `D2-C286`, `D2-C288`, `D2-C187`, `D2-C046`, `D3-C633`, `D3-C608`, `D1-C491`, `D2-C884`.

## What to do

- Audit every component that outputs links (navigation, pagination, filters, product tiles, language selectors) for a real `<a href>` to a crawlable URL.
- Replace hash routes with real paths and History API routing, and make every view that should rank reachable through an `<a href>`.
- Keep main and sub-navigation links in the server HTML so they survive a rendering failure.
- Do not count on plain-text URLs for discovery; link them properly.
- Use URL fragments only where you deliberately want filter combinations kept out of the crawl.

## What Google's documentation says

- **[Docs]** Google's link best practices say Google can generally crawl a link only if it is an a element with an href attribute, and list routerLink without href, href on a span, onclick-only a elements and javascript: URLs as not recommended, while noting that Google may still attempt to parse them.
  <br><sub>`D2-C043` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, How is HTML interpreted · is the documentation · [Link best practices for Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/links-crawlable) · Used by `DEV-URL-01`, `DEV-URL-02`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's JavaScript SEO basics guide says Googlebot extracts links twice, from the HTML response before rendering and again from the rendered HTML, so links injected with JavaScript can be found if they use crawlable `<a href>` markup.
  <br><sub>`D2-C169` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Lightning session D: Rendering and JavaScript · is the documentation · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Extends [D1-C040](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-01`</sub>

- **[Docs]** To make infinite scroll indexable, Google's lazy-loading guide says to support paginated loading: give each chunk its own persistent, unique URL, link sequentially to those URLs, and update the displayed URL with the History API when a new chunk becomes the main visible element.
  <br><sub>`D2-C276` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · is the documentation · [Fix lazy-loaded content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/lazy-loading) · Extends [D1-C115](../sessions/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-07`</sub>

## Analysis

- **[Analysis]** Google's link-extraction slide put routerLink, href on a span, onclick-only links and javascript: URLs under 'can not extract', which is stricter than Google's link documentation saying Google may still try to parse them; either way they are not dependable links for discovery.
  <br><sub>`D2-C044` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, How is HTML interpreted</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Audit every template and JavaScript component that outputs links, such as navigation, pagination, filters and product tiles: each needs a real a element with an href, because onclick handlers, routerLink without href, href on a span and javascript: URLs leave the target pages without a link Google can reliably extract.
  <br><sub>`D2-C045` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, How is HTML interpreted</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Do not rely on plain-text URLs for discovery: even if Google sometimes picks them up, a proper a href link is what was described as feeding discovery, site structure and ranking.
  <br><sub>`D2-C047` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, How is HTML interpreted</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Hash-fragment links are a problem only where Google should follow them: product, category and language links need a real URL in an `<a href>`, while fragments can deliberately keep filter combinations out of the crawl, as Google's faceted navigation guide allows.
  <br><sub>`D2-C188` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session D: Rendering and JavaScript · Extends [D1-C101](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-08`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Build market and language selectors as plain `<a href>` links to each alternate URL, not buttons or script handlers; otherwise the language versions have no internal links and depend on sitemaps to be found, which is slow.
  <br><sub>`D2-C189` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session D: Rendering and JavaScript · Extends [D1-C067](../sessions/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) · Used by `DEV-INT-06`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Audit a single-page app by searching both the templates and the rendered HTML for href="#..." routes, `<a>` elements without href and onclick navigation; every view that should rank needs an `<a href>` link to a real path.
  <br><sub>`D2-C290` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript</sub>

- **[Analysis]** With a typical refresh of about 30 days and deep or soft-404-like pages recrawled only every few months, link important deep pages from strong hub pages and fix pages that look like errors; then check recrawl intervals by site depth in server logs or the Crawl Stats report.
  <br><sub>`D3-C609` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, How long does it take to..?</sub>

## Built on these claims

The items of the developer and content kits that rest on this topic's claims.

- Requirement `DEV-CAN-09`: Keep migration redirects in place long term and judge a move in Search Console, not with site: queries
- Requirement `DEV-INT-06`: Build language and market selectors as `<a href>` links to each alternate URL
- Requirement `DEV-URL-01`: Make every navigational link an `<a>` element whose href holds a real URL
- Requirement `DEV-URL-02`: Do not navigate with onclick handlers, javascript: URLs, routerLink without href or # pseudo-links
- Requirement `DEV-URL-03`: Route single-page apps with the History API and real paths, not # fragments
- Requirement `DEV-URL-07`: Back infinite scroll and load-more buttons with paginated URLs
- Requirement `DEV-URL-08`: Keep faceted navigation out of the crawl with robots.txt rules or URL fragments
- Glossary term *Change of Address tool*
- Glossary term *History API*
- Glossary term *Single-page app (SPA)*
